To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the following two problems are equivalent (i.e., they have the same computational complexity) for (networks of ) timed automata: (i) model checking for all properties expressible in the modal -calculus and (ii) reachability checking.

the following classes of properties of timed automata are decidable: (i) the reachability problem for timed automata with one clock and two locations; (ii) the reachability of timed automata with two clocks and two locations; and (iii) the reachability and safety properties of timed automaton networks with a single clock and two locations.

the model checking of the following classes of properties can be reduced to checking reachability: (i) safety, liveness and fairness properties of timed automata; (ii) safety properties of networks of timed automata, and (iii) liveness and fairness (and thus all) properties of networks of testing automata (which are an extension of timed automata with a testing mechanism).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What are the properties of a timed system that can be checked using a timed reachability test, and what is the power of such tests?
the problem of model checking for a given class of temporal logic formulas.
the question: "Given a property of a timed automaton, is it possible to check the property by only considering the reachable states of the automaton?".
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reachability checking is the most powerful testing technique for networks of timed automata.

model checking is reducible to reachability checking if and only if the property is a conjunction of reachability properties, and the automaton is deterministic and has only a bounded number of locations.
model checking timed automata is equivalent to reachability testing for timed automata.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified the set of properties for which testing is possible and have provided an algorithm to decide whether a given property is in this class or not.

the class of properties that can be reduced to the reachability problem in timed automata is precisely the class of properties for which we can define a suitable notion of testing automata that can be reduced, by a simple syntactic transformation, to a reachability problem in the original automaton.
we show that reachability is the most powerful testing strategy for timed automata.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while model checking of timed automata is PSPACE-complete, testing timed automata for reachability is in P.
the class of properties we consider is quite large, and includes all the properties considered in the literature so far.
the class of properties for which reachability testing is decidable is much wider than what has been known so far, and in fact, it includes all safety properties and many liveness properties.
